test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 01 Sept, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The selling price of 20 books is equal to the cost price of 36 books. Find the loss or gain percentage.
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Given: **20 × SP = 36 × CP**.

Ratio of **SP/CP = 36/20 = 9/5**.

Profit = **9 − 5 = 4 units**.

Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 ⇒ (4 ÷ 5) × 100 = **80%**.

Since SP > CP, it is a **gain**.

**∴ The correct answer is 80% gain.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Selling price (SP) of 20 books = Cost price (CP) of 36 books.

**Formulas:** Profit = SP − CP | Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8a5e3e79b60b63af3114cc1957ff02d9ee5f566e65e79fcc65b7d03d70efdee5.png] 

⇒ Let the **CP of 1 book be Re. 1**.

⇒ CP of 36 books = Rs. 36.

⇒ SP of 20 books = CP of 36 books = **Rs. 36**.

⇒ CP of 20 books = Rs. 20.

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 36 − 20 = **Rs. 16**.

⇒ Profit% = (16 ÷ 20) × 100 = 4/5 × 100 = **80%**.

**∴ The correct answer is 80% gain.**

**__Additional Information__**

Cost Price and Selling Price Relation

When the quantity of items for CP and SP are different, equate the values to find the ratio of SP/CP to determine profit or loss percentage.

Profit vs Loss Percentage

If SP > CP, it is a **Gain**. If CP > SP, it is a **Loss**. Both are always calculated on the **Cost Price (CP)** unless stated otherwise.</p
